title: CSS features in the specs that ship in browsers but are missing from VS Code

atRules.name: @function
atRules.description: Defines a custom CSS function, called like a built-in one as `--name(arguments)`. Its body can declare local custom properties and returns the value of its `result` descriptor.

selectors.name: ::scroll-button
selectors.description: A browser-generated button that scrolls its scroll container. The argument picks the direction (`up`, `down`, `left`, `right`, `block-start`, `block-end`, `inline-start`, `inline-end`, or `*` for all); the button appears once it has a `content` value.

selectors.name: ::search-text
selectors.description: Styles text matched by the browser's find-in-page feature. `::search-text:current` targets the active match.

selectors.name: ::view-transition-group-children
selectors.description: Wraps the nested view transition groups of a captured element when `view-transition-group` nests them, so they can be clipped or styled together. Takes a view transition name.

selectors.name: :interest-source
selectors.description: Matches an element with `interestfor` while the user is showing interest in it, for example by hovering or focusing it.

selectors.name: :interest-target
selectors.description: Matches the target of an `interestfor` element while the user is showing interest in that element.

selectors.name: :navigation-source
selectors.description: Matches the element that started the current navigation, such as the clicked link. It reflects `NavigateEvent.sourceElement`.

selectors.name: :target-after
selectors.description: Matches scroll markers that come after the active one (the marker matching `:target-current`) in their scroll marker group.

selectors.name: :target-before
selectors.description: Matches scroll markers that come before the active one (the marker matching `:target-current`) in their scroll marker group.

selectors.name: :heading
selectors.description: Matches elements that have a heading level, such as `<h1>`–`<h6>`. The functional form `:heading(2, 3)` matches only the listed levels.
